question: Should OpenClaw adopt this as a core-owned diagnostics contract with a host-bound plugin emitter and durable operator history, or should plugin emission and the UI/query surfaces be deferred from the initial taxonomy?
rationale: The answer fixes the permanent plugin trust boundary, public SDK compatibility commitment, diagnostics ownership, and storage lifecycle; those are product and security choices rather than mechanical repairs.

options.title: Stage a core-owned contract
options.body: Land a narrower taxonomy through the existing diagnostics owner with host-bound provenance, deferring external plugin emission and operator history until their contracts are separately approved.

options.title: Approve the full platform surface
options.body: Keep the plugin API, exporters, CLI, and UI together, but require loader-derived trust, lifecycle-owned collection, durable storage design, and complete real-system proof first.

options.title: Pause the core proposal
options.body: Close or pause this PR while the canonical issue determines whether optional safety observability should instead live primarily in a plugin.

recommendation.title: Stage a core-owned contract
recommendation.body: Land a narrower taxonomy through the existing diagnostics owner with host-bound provenance, deferring external plugin emission and operator history until their contracts are separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and prior product/security review evidence make steipete the strongest routing candidate for the cross-cutting plugin and diagnostics boundary decision.
